reasoning: 1. TARGET ENGAGEMENT: Strong evidence that ADI-PEG 20 engaged its intended target - plasma arginine was depleted from baseline 49-62 μM to 2-9 μM by day 4, confirming the drug reached and modulated arginine levels as intended. 2. PATHWAY MODULATION: Clear evidence of downstream biological activity - plasma citrulline increased from 23-38 μM to 158-280 μM by day 4-15, confirming the arginine deiminase pathway was activated. Early metabolic response by PET on day 4 in 7/31 patients further supports pathway engagement. 3. CLINICAL TRANSLATION: Complete failure at the clinical endpoint level - 0/31 patients achieved complete or partial response (ORR = 0% across all three cohorts). Some patients achieved stable disease (29% overall DCR), but this represents disease stabilization rather than tumor regression. 4. POPULATION EFFECTS: ASS-negative tumors showed no improved response versus ASS ≤5% positive tumors, contradicting the hypothesis that ASS-deficient tumors would be more sensitive to arginine depletion. 5. CONFOUNDERS: This was a dose-escalation Phase I study with only 31 patients total, which may be underpowered for efficacy assessment. However, the complete absence of objective responses across all dose levels suggests the issue is not statistical power but rather biological translation.

failure_modes.evidence: Clear target engagement (arginine depletion) and pathway modulation (citrulline increase, metabolic PET changes) but complete failure to achieve objective tumor responses (0% ORR). The biology moved as predicted but did not translate to clinical benefit.
